question: how many women's colleges in the US

answer.message:
IPEDS has no "women's college" flag. How should we identify them?

**A. No men enrolled (all students)**

Count US Title IV institutions whose total fall 2024 enrollment (all students) includes zero men and at least one woman.

Proxy: IPEDS has no women's-college designation. Fall 2024 enrollment, all levels combined. Counts institutions that report zero men, which may include tiny or specialized schools that are not women's colleges, and excludes women's colleges that enroll a few men (e.g. graduate or non-degree students). Institutions with missing enrollment are excluded; the count is a proxy, not an official list.

**B. No men among undergraduates**

Count US Title IV institutions whose fall 2024 undergraduate enrollment includes zero men and at least one woman, allowing co-ed graduate programs.

Proxy: IPEDS has no women's-college designation. Fall 2024 undergraduate enrollment only; graduate programs may enroll men. Better fits traditional women's colleges with co-ed graduate programs, but may include small or specialized undergraduate programs that are not women's colleges. Institutions with missing undergraduate enrollment are excluded.

definitions.title: Level of student
definitions.long_description: Level of student Undergraduate A student enrolled in a 4- or 5-year bachelor's degree program, an associate's degree program, or a vocational or technical program below the baccalaureate. Degree/certificate-seeking students Students enrolled in courses for credit who are recognized by the institution as seeking a degree or other formal award. At the undergraduate level, this is intended to include students enrolled in vocational or occupational programs First-time student (undergraduate) A student who has no prior postsecondary experience (except as noted below) attending any institution for the first time at the undergraduate level. Includes students enrolled in academic or occupational programs . Also includes students enrolled in the fall term who attended college for the first time in the prior summer term, and students who entered with advanced standing (college credits earned before graduation from high school). Institutions that do not have a standard fall term should consider all students entering the institution between August 1 and October 31 as first-time students, provided they have no previous postsecondary experience. Transfer-in degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students - Degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students entering the reporting institution for the first time but known to have previously attended a postsecondary institution at the undergraduate level. These students may or may not have transferred credit(s). Non-degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates - Examples of non-degree/certificate-seeking students would be high school students enrolled in creditable courses prior to high school graduation, or those enrolled in creditable courses who for some reason are not seeking a degree/certificate. Graduate student A student who holds a bachelor's or first-professional degree, or equivalent, and is taking courses at the post-baccalaureate level. These students may or may not be enrolled in graduate programs . First-professional student A student enrolled in any of the following degree programs : Chiropractic (D.C. or D.C.M.) Dentistry (D.D.S. or D.M.D.) Law (L.L.B., J.D.) Medicine (M.D.) Optometry (O.D.) Osteopathic Medicine (D.O.) Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) Podiatry (D.P.M., D.P., or Pod.D.) Theology (M.Div., M.H.L., B.D., or Ordination) Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M.)
